days.grammarTitle: I'm • my / your • What's your name?
days.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to introduce themselves and ask a partner's name using I'm, my and your in at least three correct sentences.

rules: I am = I'm: I'm Fahad.
my = belongs to me • your = belongs to you
Question: What's your name? Answer: My name's Saad.
examples: Hello, I'm Ali.
What's your name?
My name's Nawaf. Nice to meet you.

reading.title: Hello! I'm Fahad
reading.text: Hello! My name is Fahad. I'm a student at IATC in Riyadh. This is my classmate. His name is Saad. Saad is from Riyadh, too. Our teacher is Mr Hamid. He is very nice. In the morning, the teacher says, 'Hello, class! How are you?' We say, 'We're fine, thanks.' Then I sit down with my partner, and we start our English lesson.
tf: The teacher's name is Mr Hamid.
Fahad sits down with his teacher.

reading2.title: How Are You Today?
reading2.text:
It is a new day at IATC. Mr Khalid is in the classroom.
"Good morning, class! How are you today?"
"We're fine, thank you!"
"Hello, Nasser. How are you?"
"I'm very well, thanks. And you?"
"I'm OK, thank you. Sit down, please."
Nasser is with his partner, Majed.
"How are you, Majed?"
"Fine, thanks."
"Is this your book?"
"Yes, it is. Thank you!"
tf: Mr Khalid is in the classroom.

Majed is in a sports shop in Riyadh. He wants a new bag and a pair of football shoes.

reading2.title: A Postcard from Abha
reading2.text:
Dear Hamza,
Greetings from Abha! I'm here with my family for a week. Abha is amazing! It's in the mountains, and the weather is wonderful. It isn't hot like Riyadh. It's only eighteen degrees in the afternoon, and at night it's cold. In the morning, the fog is beautiful, and sometimes it rains.

Khalid

reading.title: Where's My Laptop?
reading.text:
It's Sunday afternoon, and Waleed is late for college! Where are his things? His room isn't tidy.
There is a desk next to the window. On the desk, there is a lamp, an alarm clock and some books, but there isn't a laptop. Where is it?
Waleed looks under the bed. There are some trainers and a sports bag, but there isn't a laptop. Is it in the drawer? No. There are some pens and his car keys in the drawer. Are there any games on the shelf? Yes, there are some games and a DVD player, but there isn't a laptop!
Then his brother calls him: "Waleed! Your laptop is here, on the sofa in the living room!"

reading.title: Riyadh, My Home Town
reading.text:
My home town is Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia. It is a big, modern city, and it is very cosmopolitan. People from many countries live and work here.
What is there to do in Riyadh? There are excellent museums, like the National Museum. Al Masmak is an old castle in the city centre, and it is very interesting. The Kingdom Tower is spectacular at night. There are a lot of parks, malls and supermarkets, and there is entertainment for everybody.
There are restaurants with all kinds of food: Saudi, Indian, Thai and Italian. There isn't a sea in Riyadh, but the desert is near. In winter, we go camping there.
Riyadh is very hot in summer, but I love my home town!

reading.title: Is There a Bank Near Here?
reading.text:
Faisal is new in Al Malaz. He is at the bus station.
Faisal: Excuse me. Is there a bank near here?
Man: Yes, there is. Go out of the bus station and turn left. Go straight on for about five minutes. Go past the supermarket, and turn right at the traffic lights. The bank is on the corner, opposite the mosque.
Faisal: Thank you. And is there a metro station near here?
Man: Yes, there is, but it isn't very near. It's about twenty minutes on foot. Bus number 7 is quick.
Faisal: Is there a car park at the metro station?
Man: Yes, there's a big car park next to it.
Faisal: Thanks a lot!
The Riyadh Metro is new, fast and cheap. There are six lines, and the trains are clean and comfortable.

reading.title: Out of Town: The Four Seasons
reading.text:
Saudi Arabia is a big country, and there are many things to do out of town.
In winter, the weather is cool and fresh. It is a good season for camping in the desert. The sky is blue, and the nights are cold. In spring, there are some green plants and flowers in the desert. A lot of people go jogging and cycling in the parks.
Summer is very hot, so people go to the Red Sea or to the mountains in Abha and Taif. In Jeddah, there are a lot of water sports, like sailing and fishing. From Jizan, a ferry goes to the beautiful Farasan Islands.
In autumn, it is warm and sunny. My favourite season is winter. I love outdoor sports, and I go cycling with my friends every weekend.
comp: What is the weather like in winter?
Cool and fresh (and the nights are cold).
Where do people go in summer?
To the Red Sea or to the mountains in Abha and Taif.

head: Subject
Affirmative (+)
Negative (−)
Question (?)
table.note: isn't = is not      aren't = are not      We say “I'm not”, NOT “I amn't”.

grammar.overviewTitle: When Do We Use am / is / are?
overview: My bag is in the car.
rules: Affirmative (+)
Subject + am / is / are + …
He {is} a police officer.
Negative (−)
Subject + am not / isn't / aren't + …
The coffee {isn't} hot.
Yes / No question (?)
Am / Is / Are + subject + …?
{Are} you from Riyadh?  —  Yes, I am.
Wh- question (?)
Wh- word + am / is / are + subject?
Where {is} he from?  —  He's from Egypt.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ He doctor.   ✓ He {is} a doctor.      ✗ I have 19 years.   ✓ I {am} 19 years old.
grammar.watchNote: Arabic has no present-tense 'be' in sentences like هو طبيب, so students often drop it. Age uses be (I'm 19), not have. Say every example aloud and tap the table on am / is / are.

sections.title: Affirmative Sentences (+)
sections.formula: Subject  +  am / is / are  +  noun / adjective / place          I'm  •  he's  •  we're  •  they're
items: I {am} a student at college.
My name {is} Fahad.
I{'m} nineteen years old.
We {are} in class FND 68.
My father {is} a bank manager.
Cairo {is} in Egypt.
They{'re} from England.
My bag {is} on the desk.
It{'s} hot in Riyadh today.
Abha {is} beautiful.

sections.title: Negative Sentences (−)
sections.formula: Subject  +  am not / isn't / aren't  +  …
items: I{'m not} from Jeddah.
He {isn't} late today.
My house {isn't} big.
We {aren't} at home now.
The coffee {isn't} hot.
They {aren't} from Spain.
My brother {isn't} a doctor. He's a nurse.
It {isn't} cold in Riyadh in September.
You {aren't} late for class.
The shops {aren't} open.

sections.title: Yes / No Questions (?)
sections.formula: Am / Is / Are  +  subject  +  …?      Short answer:  Yes, I am.  /  No, it isn't.
items: {Are} you a student? — Yes, I am.
{Is} he from Egypt? — Yes, he is.
{Is} your house big? — No, it isn't. It's small.
{Are} they from England? — No, they aren't. They're from Canada.
{Is} the coffee hot? — Yes, it is.
{Are} we in class FND 68? — Yes, we are.
{Is} your father a doctor? — No, he isn't. He's a teacher.
{Is} Fahad from Jeddah? — No, he isn't. He's from Riyadh.
{Are} you tired? — Yes, I am.
{Is} London in England? — Yes, it is.

sections.title: Wh- Questions (?)
sections.formula: Wh- word  +  am / is / are  +  subject  +  …?          What's = What is      Where's = Where is
items: What{'s} your name? — My name's Khalid.
Where {are} you from? — I'm from Saudi Arabia.
How old {are} you? — I'm nineteen.
Who {is} your English teacher? — Mr Adel is my teacher.
How {are} you? — I'm fine, thanks.
What{'s} this in English? — It's a camera.
What{'s} your job? — I'm a student.
Where{'s} your house? — It's near the college.
What colour {is} your car? — It's white.
How many students {are} in your class? — There are 28 students.

practice: They ____ from Spain. They're from Italy.
____ he from Egypt?  Yes, he is.
We ____ at home. We are in class.
The coffee ____ hot. It is cold.

grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the present simple (verb / verb-s, don't / doesn't, do / does) and the adverbs of frequency always, usually, often, sometimes, hardly ever and never in the correct position to talk about daily routines, free time, food and likes, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.

head: Subject
Affirmative (+)
Negative (−)
Question (?)
table.note: don't = do not      doesn't = does not      After don't / doesn't / do / does → verb with NO -s:  He doesn't play.  Does he play?

grammar.overviewTitle: When Do We Use the Present Simple?
overview: I get up at six every day.
rules: Affirmative (+)
I / you / we / they + verb      he / she / it + verb-s
She {gets} up at seven o'clock.
Negative (−)
Subject + don't / doesn't + verb
He {doesn't} eat meat.
Yes / No question (?)
Do / Does + subject + verb …?
{Do} you like tennis?  —  Yes, I do.
Wh- question (?)
Wh- word + do / does + subject + verb?
What time {does} he get home?  —  At six.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ I am like tea.   ✓ I {like} tea.      ✗ She get up at 7.   ✓ She {gets} up at 7.
grammar.watchNote: Three common errors: (1) adding 'am / is / are' before a present-simple verb (I am like); (2) forgetting -s with he / she / it (She get up); (3) the adverb in the wrong place (✗ I go always to bed at 11 → ✓ I always go to bed at 11). Also: no -s after doesn't / does (✗ He doesn't plays).

sections.title: Affirmative Sentences (+)
sections.formula: I / You / We / They  +  verb          He / She / It  +  verb-s
items: I {get up} at six o'clock every day.
My father {leaves} home at seven.
We {have} lunch at one o'clock.
He {has} a shower in the morning.
My brother {plays} tennis on Monday.
My aunt {speaks} Arabic and French.
My mother {watches} a drama on TV.
They {live} in a flat in Riyadh.
He {studies} English on the Internet.
My uncle {goes} shopping at the weekend.

sections.title: Negative Sentences (−)
sections.formula: I / You / We / They  +  don't  +  verb          He / She / It  +  doesn't  +  verb
items: I {don't} like Coke.
He {doesn't} eat meat.
We {don't} go to college on Friday.
My father {doesn't} drink coffee.
They {don't} live in a big house.
She {doesn't} speak Spanish.
I {don't} watch TV in the morning.
The bus {doesn't} stop here.
My brother {doesn't} get up early.
We {don't} have lunch at home.

sections.title: Yes / No Questions (?)
sections.formula: Do / Does  +  subject  +  verb …?      Short answer:  Yes, I do.  /  No, he doesn't.
items: {Do} you like pizza? — Yes, I do. I love it!
{Does} your father work all day? — Yes, he does.
{Do} you play tennis? — No, I don't. I play football.
{Does} she speak Japanese? — No, she doesn't.
{Do} you live in a flat? — Yes, I do.
{Does} your mother cook kabsa? — Yes, she does. It's delicious!
{Do} they go out on Thursday? — Yes, they do.
{Does} the bus stop here? — No, it doesn't.
{Do} you have breakfast at home? — Yes, I do.
{Does} your brother drive to work? — No, he doesn't. He takes a taxi.

sections.title: Wh- Questions (?)
sections.formula: Wh- word  +  do / does  +  subject  +  verb …?
items: What time {do} you get up? — I get up at six o'clock.
What {do} you have for breakfast? — Eggs, toast and tea.
Where {does} your aunt live? — She lives in Jeddah.
What time {does} your father get home? — At five o'clock.
What {do} you do at the weekend? — I visit my family and relax.
How many languages {do} you speak? — Two: Arabic and English.
What {does} your brother do? — He's a waiter. He works in a restaurant.
When {do} you go to bed? — At eleven o'clock.
What sports {do} you like? — I like swimming and football.
Who {cooks} dinner in your house? — My mother cooks dinner.

sections.title: Adverbs of Frequency: 10 Examples
sections.formula: Subject  +  adverb  +  verb …          Subject  +  am / is / are  +  adverb …
items: I {always} have a shower in the morning.
My mother {usually} cooks kabsa on Friday.
We {often} play football after college.
My brother {sometimes} drives me to work.
He {hardly ever} eats chocolate.
I {never} drink coffee at night.
I'm {always} busy on Sunday.
My father is {never} late for work.
We {usually} go shopping at the weekend.
They {often} watch TV in the evening.

sections.title: How Often …? Questions and Answers
sections.formula: How often  +  do / does  +  subject  +  verb …?      every day • once a week • twice a week • on Fridays
items: How often {do} you play football? — Twice a week.
How often {does} he go shopping? — Once a week, on Thursday.
How often {do} you visit your uncle? — Every Friday.
How often {do} you eat pizza? — Hardly ever. I like kabsa!
How often {does} your mother cook? — Every day.
How often {do} they go to the beach? — Two or three times a year.
How often {do} you watch TV? — Sometimes, in the evening.
How often {does} the bus come? — Every twenty minutes.
How often {do} you have English? — Five days a week.
How often {does} your brother go out? — Once or twice a week.

practice: ____ you like pizza?  Yes, I do.
____ your father work all day?  No, he doesn't.
What time ____ he go to bed?
Add never:  He drinks coffee at night.
He never drinks coffee at night.
Add always:  I am busy on Sunday.
I am always busy on Sunday.
How ____ do you go shopping?  Once a week.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the form table (items 1–7) or the 'Where does the adverb go?' slide (items 8–10) and redo the items they missed.

bullets: when you get up and have breakfast
what you do in the afternoon
what you usually do at the weekend
exit.frame: I always get up at ____. I usually have ____ for breakfast. In the afternoon, I ____. At the weekend, I sometimes ____.

head: Subject
Possessive adj.
Possessive pronoun
Example
rows: We have a cat. Its name is Max.
table.note: its = belongs to it (no apostrophe)      it's = it is      Possessive adjective + noun:  my phone.   Possessive pronoun alone:  mine.

Adel is {Fatima's} husband.
Possessive pronoun
mine / yours / his / hers / ours / theirs  (no noun after)
The black bag is {mine}.
Whose …?
Whose + noun + is this / are these?
{Whose} phone is this?  —  It's Talal's.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ This is mine phone.  ✓ This is {my} phone.     ✗ the son of Adel  ✓ {Adel's} son
grammar.watchNote: Arabic shows possession with a suffix (هاتفي) or with idafa (ابن عادل), so students often say 'the son of Adel' or 'mine phone'. Practise: in English the owner comes first (Adel's son). Also: 's can mean is (He's my brother = He is) or show possession (Talal's bag). Context tells you which.

sections.title: Possessive Adjectives + Noun
sections.formula: my  /  your  /  his  /  her  /  its  /  our  /  their   +   noun
items: This is {my} family tree.
{Your} English book is on the desk.
My brother is 21. {His} name is Turki.
My aunt is a doctor. {Her} hospital is big.
We have a white cat. {Its} name is Max.
{Our} house is near the college.
My uncles live in Jeddah. {Their} flat is big.
Talal and Rasha love {their} parents.
What's {your} phone number?
My father reads {his} newspaper every day.

sections.title: Possessive 's: Fatima's Family
sections.formula: Name / noun  +  's  +  noun          Plural owner (-s):  my parents' house
items: Adel is {Fatima's} husband.
Fatima is {Adel's} wife.
Talal is {Adel's} son.
Rasha is {Fatima's} daughter.
{Adel's} office is in the city.
My {father's} car is white.
My {brother's} name is Fahad.
My {uncle's} company is very big.
The {teacher's} desk is next to the board.
My {parents'} house is near the park.

sections.title: Possessive Pronouns
sections.formula: mine  /  yours  /  his  /  hers  /  ours  /  theirs        (NO noun after)
items: This phone is {mine}.
Is this pen {yours}?
The black car is {his}.
The red bag is {hers}.
This classroom is {ours}.
The big house is {theirs}.
My car is white. {Yours} is black.
These shoes aren't {mine}.
This book isn't {yours}. It's {mine}.
Your phone is new. {Mine} is old.

sections.title: Whose …? Questions
sections.formula: Whose  +  noun  +  is this / are these?        Answer:  It's Talal's.  /  It's mine.
items: {Whose} phone is this? — It's mine.
{Whose} bag is this? — It's Talal's.
{Whose} shoes are these? — They're my brother's.
{Whose} book is on the desk? — It's the teacher's.
{Whose} car is that? — It's my father's.
Is this {your} pen? — Yes, it's mine.
Is this {his} jacket? — No, it isn't. It's mine.
What's {your} father's job? — He's an accountant.
What's {your} best friend's name? — His name is Abdullah.
Where's {their} house? — It's near the bank.

sections.title: have / has: Family and Things
sections.formula: I / you / we / they  +  have          he / she / it  +  has          −  don't have / doesn't have
items: I {have} two brothers and a sister.
Adel and Fatima {have} two children.
My uncle {has} a big house.
We {have} a new teacher.
My best friend {has} a lot of friends.
My cousin {has} a part-time job.
They {have} a white cat.
I {don't have} a car.
My brother {doesn't have} a job yet.
{Do} you {have} a laptop?  —  Yes, I do.

practice: My brother is 21. ____ name is Turki.
We are a big family. ____ house is big.
Is this book ____? (you)  Yes, it's mine.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the possessives table (items 1–8) or the have / has slide (items 9–10) and redo the items they missed.

bullets: how many brothers and sisters you have
exit.frame: My father's name is ____. He is a ____. I have ____ brothers and ____ sisters. My best friend's name is ____.
exit.model: My father's name is Saleh. He is an accountant. I have two brothers and one sister. My best friend's name is Abdullah. He is funny. (25 words)

grammar.title: Plurals & There is / are
grammar.sub: rooms  •  There are some pens.  •  Are there any …?
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to form regular and irregular plurals and use there is / there are with some / any and How many …? to talk about rooms, furniture and their home town, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: make plurals with -s, -es, -ies and -ves.
use irregular plurals: men, people, children.
say what is in a room with there is / are.
use some (+) and any (− and ?).
ask and answer How many … are there?
write about my home in about 25 words.
warmup: How many rooms are there in your house?
Is there a park near your house?

head: Number
Affirmative (+)
Negative (−)
Question (?)
table.note: There's = There is      some → + sentences      any → − and ? sentences      a / an → one thing

rules: Plural noun
noun + s / es / ies / ves   (or irregular)
two {rooms},  three {buses},  five {people}
There is / There are
There is + a / an + one thing   •   There are + plural
{There are} four bedrooms in our house.
some (+)
There are some + plural noun
There are {some} pens in the drawer.
any (− and ?)
There aren't any …  /  Are there any …?
{Are there any} books?  —  No, there aren't.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ There is two bedrooms.  ✓ {There are} two bedrooms.      ✗ two childs  ✓ two {children}
grammar.watchNote: Arabic uses يوجد for one thing and for many things, so students say 'There is two …'. Count the noun first: one → is, two or more → are. Irregular plurals never take -s (✗ childs, ✗ peoples).

sections.title: Plural Nouns
sections.formula: room → rooms      bus → buses      city → cities      shelf → shelves      man → men
items: Our flat has five {rooms}.
There are two {bathrooms} in our house.
The {walls} in my bedroom are white.
My {car keys} are on the table.
Riyadh and Jeddah are big {cities}.
The {buses} stop near the station.
The books are on the {shelves}.
There are many {people} in the park.
Three {men} work in the supermarket.
My uncle has four {children}.

sections.title: There is / There are: My Home
sections.formula: There is  +  a / an  +  singular noun          There are  +  plural noun
items: {There is} a sofa in the living room.
{There are} four bedrooms in our house.
{There is} a cooker in the kitchen.
{There are} two lamps next to the bed.
{There is} an armchair in my room.
{There are} some posters on the wall.
{There is} a big park in my home town.
{There are} many restaurants in Riyadh.
{There is} a library near the college.
{There are} 28 students in our class.

sections.title: some / any
sections.formula: +   There are some …          −   There aren't any …          ?   Are there any …?
items: There are {some} pens in the drawer.
There aren't {any} books on the desk.
There is {some} water in the fridge.
There isn't {any} milk in the fridge.
I have {some} new computer games.
We don't have {any} homework today.
There are {some} good shops in my town.
There aren't {any} mountains in Riyadh.
I want {some} tea, please.
He doesn't have {any} money.

sections.title: Is there …? / Are there any …? / How many …?
sections.formula: Is there a …?  Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.       Are there any …?  Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.
items: {Is there} a TV in your bedroom? — No, there isn't.
{Are there} any pens in the drawer? — Yes, there are.
{Is there} a garden at your house? — Yes, there is.
{Are there} any posters on the wall? — No, there aren't.
{Is there} any water in the fridge? — Yes, there is.
{Are there} any parks near your house? — Yes, there are two.
{Is there} a supermarket near here? — Yes, there is. It's on the left.
{How many} rooms are there in your flat? — There are five.
{How many} people are there in your family? — There are seven.
{Are there} any museums in Riyadh? — Yes, there are. The National Museum!

practice: There ____ four bedrooms in our house.
There ____ a sofa in the living room.
There are ____ pens in the drawer. (+)
Are there ____ books?  No, there aren't.
How ____ rooms are there?  There are six.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the plural spelling rules (items 1–5) or the there is / are table (items 6–10) and redo the items they missed.

bullets: what there is in your bedroom
what there is near your home
exit.frame: I live in a ____. There are ____ rooms. In my bedroom, there is a ____ and some ____. Near my home, there is a ____.
exit.model: I live in a flat in Riyadh. There are five rooms. In my bedroom, there is a desk and some books. Near my home, there is a park. (28 words)

grammar.title: Place & Time Prepositions
grammar.sub: in  •  on  •  under  •  next to      at  •  on  •  in
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use in, on, under, next to, between, behind, in front of and opposite for place, at home / at work, and at, on, in for time, correctly in sentences and in Where …? / When …? questions about their home, town and week, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: say where things are: in, on, under, next to.
use between, behind, in front of, opposite.
use at home, at work, at college.
use at, on, in with times, days, months, seasons.
ask and answer Where …? and When …?
write about my week in about 25 words.
warmup: What time do you get up?
What do you do at the weekend?

head: Preposition
Place
Time
Arabic
table.note: Time:  at + clock time, night, the weekend      on + day, date      in + month, season, year, the morning / afternoon / evening

rules: Place: in / on / under
in = inside   •   on = on top   •   under = below
The pens are {in} the drawer.
Place: next to / between / opposite
next to = beside   •   between = in the middle of two
The bank is {between} the café and the hotel.
Time: at / on
at + clock time, night, the weekend   •   on + day, date
I get up {at} 6 o'clock {on} Sunday.
Time: in
in + month, season, year, the morning
It's very hot {in} summer.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ in Sunday  ✓ {on} Sunday     ✗ on 8 o'clock  ✓ {at} 8 o'clock     ✗ in night  ✓ {at} night
grammar.watchNote: Arabic uses في for in, on and at with time (في يوم الأحد، في الساعة الثامنة), so students choose 'in' for everything. Draw the time triangle: at (small: clock time) → on (days, dates) → in (big: months, seasons, years, parts of the day). Places: at home / at work / at college (no 'the'), but in Riyadh, in the kitchen.

sections.title: Place: in / on / under / next to …
sections.formula: in   •   on   •   under   •   next to   •   between   •   behind   •   in front of   •   opposite
items: The water is {in} the fridge.
My laptop is {on} the desk.
The DVD player is {under} the TV.
The lamp is {next to} the bed.
The cat is {behind} the sofa.
My car keys are {in} the drawer.
The bank is {between} the café and the hotel.
The bus stops {in front of} the museum.
The supermarket is {opposite} the park.
There are some posters {on} the wall.

sections.title: Time: at / on / in
sections.formula: at + time          on + day / date          in + month / season / year / the morning
items: I get up {at} six o'clock.
We have English {on} Sunday.
Progress Exam 2 is {in} October.
I study {in} the afternoon.
The bus comes {at} half past seven.
We visit my grandfather {on} Friday.
I relax {at} the weekend.
It's very hot {in} summer.
We go to the desert {in} winter.
Saudi National Day is {on} 23 September.

sections.title: Where …? Questions
sections.formula: Where is / are + noun?        →        It's / They're  +  in / on / under / next to …    •    at home / at work
items: {Where} is my phone? — It's on the sofa.
{Where} are my car keys? — They're in the drawer.
{Where} is the cat? — It's under the bed.
{Where} is the bank? — It's between the café and the hotel.
{Where} do you live? — I live in a flat in Riyadh.
{Where} is your father? — He's at work.
{Where} are your brothers? — They're at home.
{Where} do you study? — I study at college.
{Where} is the bus station? — It's opposite the supermarket.
{Where} is the lamp? — It's next to the bed.

sections.title: When …? / What time …? Questions
sections.formula: When / What time  +  is / do / does  …?        →        at / on / in  …
items: {When} is Progress Exam 2? — It's in October.
{What time} do you get up? — At six o'clock.
{When} do you play football? — On Friday.
{When} do you study English? — In the afternoon.
{What time} does the bus come? — At half past seven.
{When} is Saudi National Day? — It's on 23 September.
{When} do you relax? — At the weekend.
{When} is it cold in Riyadh? — In winter.
{When} do you do your homework? — In the evening.
{What time} do you go to bed? — At eleven o'clock.

practice: The bank is ____ the café and the hotel.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the place rules (items 1–5) or the time triangle (items 6–10) and redo the items they missed.

exit.frame: I get up at ____. On Friday, I ____. I study at ____ in the ____.
exit.model: I get up at six o'clock. On Friday, I visit my grandfather. I study at college in the afternoon from Sunday to Thursday. (23 words)

grammar.title: Past of Be: was / were
grammar.sub: was  •  were  •  wasn't  •  weren't  •  was born
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use was / were, was born and there was / there were with past time words (yesterday, last week, ago, in 2015, when I was a child) correctly in affirmative sentences, negative sentences, Yes / No questions and Wh- questions about yesterday and their childhood, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: use was (I, he, she, it) and were (you, we, they).
use yesterday, last …, … ago, in 2015.
make negatives with wasn't and weren't.
ask and answer Was / Were …? and Wh- questions.
say where and when I was born.
write about my childhood in about 25 words.
warmup: Were you at home last night?

head: Subject
Affirmative (+)
Negative (−)
Question (?)
table.note: am / is → was      are → were      Time words:  yesterday  •  last night / week / year  •  two days ago  •  in 2015  •  when I was a child

rules: Affirmative (+)
Subject + was / were + …
I {was} at home yesterday.
Negative (−)
Subject + wasn't / weren't + …
The exam {wasn't} difficult.
Yes / No question (?)
Was / Were + subject + …?
{Were} you at college last week?  —  Yes, I was.
Wh- question (?)
Wh- word + was / were + subject?
Where {were} you born?  —  In Riyadh.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ I were tired.  ✓ I {was} tired.     ✗ I born in 2007.  ✓ I {was born} in 2007.
grammar.watchNote: Link to the present: I am → I was; he is → he was; they are → they were. 'born' always needs was / were (✗ I born). 'ago' comes AFTER the time phrase (two years ago, NOT ago two years), unlike Arabic قبل سنتين.

sections.title: Affirmative Sentences (+)
sections.formula: I / He / She / It  +  was          You / We / They  +  were          + yesterday / last … / … ago
items: I {was} at home yesterday.
We {were} at college last Sunday.
My grandfather {was} a teacher.
It {was} very hot yesterday.
My friends {were} at the park last night.
I {was} in secondary school in 2024.
Our house {was} small when I was a child.
The shops {were} open last night.
The exam {was} easy.
My brothers {were} in Jeddah last week.

sections.title: Negative Sentences (−)
sections.formula: Subject  +  wasn't (was not)  /  weren't (were not)  +  …
items: I {wasn't} at home yesterday.
The exam {wasn't} difficult.
We {weren't} late for class.
My father {wasn't} at work on Saturday.
The shops {weren't} open at 6 a.m.
It {wasn't} cold last winter.
They {weren't} at the football match.
My grandfather {wasn't} rich.
The bus {wasn't} on time this morning.
My friends {weren't} tired.

sections.title: Yes / No Questions (?)
sections.formula: Was / Were  +  subject  +  …?        Short answer:  Yes, I was.  /  No, they weren't.
items: {Were} you at college yesterday? — Yes, I was.
{Was} the exam easy? — Yes, it was.
{Was} your grandfather a teacher? — No, he wasn't. He was a farmer.
{Were} the shops open? — No, they weren't.
{Was} it hot in Riyadh yesterday? — Yes, it was. It was 40 degrees!
{Were} they at the match last night? — Yes, they were.
{Was} your first school big? — No, it wasn't. It was small.
{Were} you tired last night? — Yes, I was.
{Was} the bus late this morning? — No, it wasn't.
{Were} your friends at the mall? — Yes, they were.

sections.title: Wh- Questions (?)
sections.formula: Wh- word  +  was / were  +  subject  +  …?
items: Where {were} you yesterday? — I was at home.
Where {were} you born? — I was born in Riyadh.
When {were} you born? — In 2007.
Who {was} your first teacher? — Mr Ali was my first teacher.
How {was} the exam? — It was easy.
Why {were} you late? — Because the bus was late.
What {was} your grandfather's job? — He was a farmer.
Where {were} you two years ago? — I was in secondary school.
What {was} the weather like yesterday? — It was hot and sunny.
How old {were} you in 2020? — I was thirteen.

sections.title: was born  •  there was / there were
sections.formula: was / were born  +  in + place / year          There was + singular          There were + plural
items: I {was born} in Riyadh in 2007.
My father {was born} in Abha.
My grandfather {was born} in a village.
Where {were} you {born}?
{There was} a small shop near my house.
{There were} 30 students in my class.
{There wasn't} a park in my village.
{There weren't} any big buildings in 1950.
{Was there} a school in your village?
{There were} a lot of people at the mall.

practice: The exam ____ easy. It was difficult.
____ you at college yesterday?  Yes, I was.
The shops ____ open. They were closed.
I was in Jeddah two weeks ____.
We were at the park ____ Friday.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the was / were table (items 1–6) or the past time words slide (items 7–10) and redo the items they missed.

exit.prompt: Write about when you were a child.
bullets: where and when you were born
your house when you were a child
your first school and your teacher
exit.frame: I was born in ____ in ____. My house was ____. My first school was ____. My teacher was ____.
exit.model: I was born in Riyadh in 2007. My house was small and old. My first school was near my house. My teacher was kind. (24 words)

grammar.title: The Past Simple
grammar.sub: visited  •  went  •  didn't go  •  Did you go?
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use regular and irregular past simple verbs correctly in affirmative sentences, negative sentences, Yes / No questions and Wh- questions, and tell a short story with first, then, after that and finally, about their last weekend, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: add -ed to regular verbs: visited, studied, stopped.
use irregular verbs: went, had, saw, got up …
make negatives with didn't + verb.
ask Did …? and Wh- + did questions.
tell a story with first, then, after that.
write about my last weekend in about 25 words.
warmup: Where did you go last weekend?
What did you have for breakfast?
Did you watch football last night?

head: Subject
Affirmative (+)
Negative (−)
Question (?)
table.note: The SAME form for all subjects.   didn't = did not.   After didn't / did → base verb:   ✗ didn't went   ✓ didn't go

rules: Affirmative (+)
Subject + verb-ed  /  irregular past
I {visited} my uncle. We {went} to Abha.
Negative (−)
Subject + didn't + base verb
I {didn't} watch TV last night.
Yes / No question (?)
Did + subject + base verb …?
{Did} you have a good time?  —  Yes, I did.
Wh- question (?)
Wh- word + did + subject + base verb?
Where {did} you go?  —  I went to Jeddah.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ I didn't went.  ✓ I didn't {go}.     ✗ Did you saw?  ✓ Did you {see}?     ✗ I goed.  ✓ I {went}.
grammar.watchNote: After didn't / did the verb goes back to its base form (go, see, have). Irregular verbs never take -ed (goed, eated). Time words: yesterday, last …, … ago, in 2025.

sections.title: Affirmative Sentences (+)
sections.formula: Regular:  verb + ed  (visited, studied)          Irregular:  went, had, saw, got up …
items: I {studied} English yesterday.
We {visited} my grandfather last Friday.
My brother {cooked} dinner last night.
I {got up} late on Saturday.
We {went} to the beach in Jeddah.
I {had} breakfast at seven o'clock.
My father {bought} a new car last month.
We {saw} a football match on TV.
My friends {came} to my house.
We {had} a great time!

sections.title: Negative Sentences (−)
sections.formula: Subject  +  didn't (did not)  +  base verb
items: I {didn't} watch TV last night.
We {didn't} go to college on Friday.
He {didn't} have breakfast this morning.
My brother {didn't} play football.
They {didn't} come to the match.
I {didn't} get up early on Saturday.
We {didn't} stay at a hotel.
My father {didn't} buy a new phone.
I {didn't} see my friends last week.
The bus {didn't} stop at the station.

sections.title: Yes / No Questions (?)
sections.formula: Did  +  subject  +  base verb …?        Short answer:  Yes, I did.  /  No, he didn't.
items: {Did} you have a good weekend? — Yes, I did. It was great!
{Did} you go to the beach? — No, I didn't. I went to the park.
{Did} he watch the match? — Yes, he did.
{Did} they stay at a hotel? — No, they didn't. They stayed with family.
{Did} you have breakfast this morning? — Yes, I did.
{Did} your mother cook kabsa? — Yes, she did. It was delicious!
{Did} you go shopping last week? — Yes, I did. I bought a jacket.
{Did} your brother drive to Abha? — No, he didn't. He went by bus.
{Did} you see your friends at the mall? — Yes, I did.
{Did} you study English yesterday? — Yes, I did.

sections.title: Wh- Questions (?)
sections.formula: Wh- word  +  did  +  subject  +  base verb …?
items: Where {did} you go last weekend? — I went to Jeddah.
What {did} you have for breakfast? — I had eggs and toast.
What time {did} you get up? — I got up at nine o'clock.
Who {did} you meet at the mall? — I met my cousins.
How {did} you go to Jeddah? — We went by car.
What {did} you buy? — I bought a new jacket.
When {did} you get home? — At eleven o'clock.
What {did} you watch on TV? — I watched a football match.
Why {did} you stay at home? — Because I was tired.
What {did} you do last night? — I did my homework.

sections.title: My Weekend: A Story in 10 Sentences
sections.formula: First, …      Then …      After that, …      Finally, …
items: Last Friday, I {got up} at nine o'clock.
{First}, I {had} breakfast with my family.
{Then} I {went} to the mosque.
{After that}, we {visited} my grandfather.
My aunt {made} kabsa for lunch.
In the afternoon, I {played} football.
{Then} my brother {drove} us to the mall.
We {bought} some new clothes.
We {had} dinner in a restaurant.
{Finally}, we {got} home at eleven.

practice: We ____ (go) to the beach last Friday.
____ you have a good weekend?  Yes, I did.
We had lunch. ____ that, we went home.
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the -ed spelling and irregular verb slides (items 1–4, 8–9) or the patterns slide (items 5–7) and redo the items they missed.

bullets: what you did first and then
exit.frame: Last weekend, I went to ____. I met ____. First, we ____. Then we ____.
exit.model: Last weekend, I went to my uncle's farm. I met my cousins there. First, we played football. Then we had kabsa for dinner. It was great! (26 words)

grammar.title: Articles a / an / the
grammar.sub: a coat  •  an apple  •  the station  •  Riyadh
grammar.smart: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to choose a, an, the or no article correctly with jobs, shopping, places in town, meals and names, and change a → the in a short text, with at least 8 of 10 practice items correct.
objectives: use a / an with one thing and with jobs.
choose a or an by the first sound.
use the when we know which one.
use no article with names, meals, languages.
change a → the in a short story.
write about my favourite shop in about 25 words.
warmup: What do you have for breakfast?
Is there a mall near your house?

head: Article
Use it for
Examples
Arabic
table.note: a / an + ONE thing (singular)      the + singular or plural      ✗ a books   ✓ books   ✓ the books

grammar.overviewTitle: a / an or the? Six Uses
rules: a + consonant sound
a + b, c, d, f, g … (and u = /juː/)
{a} coat,  {a} ticket,  {a} university
an + vowel sound
an + a, e, i, o, u (and silent h)
{an} apple,  {an} egg,  {an} hour
the
we know which one • only one • second time
Close {the} door, please.
No article
names, cities, countries, meals, languages, general
I live in Riyadh. I like tea.
grammar.watch: Watch out!   ✗ He is engineer.  ✓ He is {an} engineer.      ✗ I like the coffee.  ✓ I like coffee.
grammar.watchNote: Arabic has no word for a / an (هو مهندس), so students drop it: always use a / an with a job. Arabic uses ال for things in general (أحب القهوة), so students say 'I like the coffee'. In English, things in general have NO article: I like coffee. Football is exciting.

sections.title: a / an: One Thing, Jobs, How Often
sections.formula: a / an  +  one (singular) noun          jobs:  He's a waiter.          a = every:  twice a week
items: I have {a} new coat.
My brother is {an} engineer.
I want {a} return ticket, please.
I eat {an} apple every day.
My father is {a} bank manager.
Can I have {a} packet of aspirin?
There is {an} Internet café near here.
I need {a} stamp for this postcard.
We have English five days {a} week.
It's {an} expensive jacket.

sections.title: the: We Know Which One
sections.formula: the + the one we know          the + only one          a … (first time)  →  the … (second time)
items: Close {the} door, please.
{The} sun is very hot in summer.
{The} Red Sea is beautiful.
Where is {the} railway station?
{The} shops open at four.
I have a cat. {The} cat is white.
Where are {the} changing rooms?
{The} Post Office opens at eight.
My father reads {the} newspaper.
{The} bank is next to the hotel.

sections.title: No Article: 10 Examples
sections.formula: No article  +  names • cities • countries • languages • meals • things in general • by bus / at home
items: I live in {Riyadh}.
My cousin is from {Egypt}.
We speak {Arabic} at home.
I have {breakfast} at seven o'clock.
I love {Saudi coffee}.
{Football} is exciting.
I go to college by {bus}.
My father is at {work}.
{Shoes} are expensive in this shop.
We have {lunch} at home on Friday.

sections.title: At the Mall: a → the
sections.formula: First time:  a / an  +  noun          Second time (now we know it):  the  +  noun
items: There is {a} new mall in my town.
In the mall, there is {a} café and {a} bookshop.
{The} café is next to {the} bookshop.
I buy {a} coffee in {the} café.
Then I see {a} jacket and {a} hat.
{The} jacket is black. {The} hat is white.
I try on {the} jacket.
{The} jacket is 300 riyals!
I buy {the} hat. It's only 50 riyals.
Then I take {a} taxi home.

practice: I have a cat. ____ cat is white.
We have ____ lunch at one o'clock.
Excuse me, where is ____ Post Office?
grammar.practiceTarget: Target: 8 / 10 or more. Students with fewer than 8 correct: go back to the 'a or an?' slide (items 1, 2, 7, 9), the 'Six Uses' slide (items 3, 4, 6, 10) or the 'No Article' slide (items 5, 8) and redo the items they missed.

bullets: what the shop is and where it is
what there is next to it
exit.frame: My favourite shop is a ____ in ____. It is next to a ____. The ____ are ____. I usually buy ____ there.
exit.model: My favourite shop is a bookshop in the mall. It is next to a café. The books are cheap. I usually buy a book and a coffee there. (28 words)

Your father is my **uncle**, so you are my **cousin**!

**Pardon**? Half past four or quarter past four?
Half past four. But please come at four o'clock.
Hello, Nawaf. Bring a [[white]] **T-shirt** and black **shorts**.
Sorry, Coach. Can you say that again **slowly**?
Thank you. Faisal, what's your **phone number**?
Zero five five, seven three two, four one nine eight. Is that right?

dialogues.title: Hurry Up! We're Boarding!
dialogues.setting: King Khalid International Airport. Saud is at the gate. Hamad is at security.
lines: Hamad, where are you? I'm waiting at **Gate** [[12]].
I'm coming! I'm standing in the **queue** at **security**.
I know. An officer is checking my bag.
Yes, it is. And this is my **boarding pass**.
Thank you. You can go. Your flight is **on time**.
Saud, I'm walking to the gate now.
Look outside! A plane is **taking off**, and another plane is **landing**.
And the **cabin crew** are walking to our plane.
"Flight [[1020]] to [[Jeddah]] is now boarding." That's us!

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 6/FND_68_Week_6_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 6 conversation: Hurry Up! We're Boarding!

dialogues.title: Our Winter Plans
dialogues.setting: Two brothers at home on a cool October evening.
lines: Winter is coming! The weather is **cool** now.
I love **winter**. **Summer** in Riyadh is too hot.
What are you **going to** do next month?
I'm going to go **camping** in the desert with our cousins.
Great! Are you going to take **blankets**?
Yes. The nights are cold. And I'm going to cook dinner outside.
Check the **forecast** first. Sometimes there is a **dust storm**.
In January, I'm going to visit [[Tabuk]].
Yes, and sometimes there is **snow** on the mountains!

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 6/FND_68_Week_6_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 6 conversation: Our Winter Plans

dialogues.title: What Do You Do at the Weekend?
dialogues.setting: The canteen at the break on Sunday.
lines: Turki, what do you **usually** do at the **weekend**?
On Friday, I **always** go to the **mosque** with my father. Then we **visit** my **grandparents**.
Yes. My mother usually **cooks** a big **meal**: [[rice and chicken]].
Nice. On Saturday, I **often** **go shopping** with my brother.
I **sometimes** **have lunch out** with my cousins.
Do you **stay at home** on Saturday evening?
Me too. I usually **go for a walk** in the **park**.
Let's **meet** in the park this Saturday.
Good idea. We can have a **picnic**!
Great. I can bring [[tea and dates]].

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 7/FND_68_Week_7_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 7 conversation: What Do You Do at the Weekend?

dialogues.title: Where Were You Yesterday?
dialogues.setting: The workshop. Mr. Nasser, the instructor, talks to Ali and Sami.
lines: Ali, you **weren't** at the **safety** **meeting** **yesterday**. Where **were** you?
I'm sorry, Mr. Nasser. I **was** **ill**. I was [[at home]].
OK. Please send me an **email** with the **reason**.
I was there. [[Majed]] and the **engineer**, Mr. Khalid, were there too.
No, he **wasn't**. He was at the **hospital** with his father.
They weren't there. They were on **holiday** in [[Abha]].
No, it wasn't. It was only [[one hour]].
The next meeting is on Tuesday at ten o'clock in the **workshop**. Please be on time.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 7/FND_68_Week_7_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 7 conversation: Where Were You Yesterday?

dialogues.title: A Real Mechanic!
dialogues.setting: A phone call on Saturday night.
lines: Hi Saleh! I **phoned** you this morning, but you didn't answer.
Sorry! I was very busy. I **helped** my father in the **garage**.
We **washed** his car and **cleaned** the windows. Then we **changed** the **oil**.
Wow! Did you check the **engine** too?
Yes, we **checked** it. One **tyre** was flat, so we **repaired** it.
Ha ha. In the afternoon, I **carried** some boxes for our **neighbour**.
He **thanked** me and gave me some [[dates]].
Did you study in the evening?
Yes, I **studied** English and **tried** a practice test. I **finished** at [[ten]].

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 7/FND_68_Week_7_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 7 conversation: A Real Mechanic!

dialogues.title: Dinner at Najd Village
dialogues.setting: Najd Village restaurant in Riyadh. Two cousins have dinner.
lines: Good evening. Welcome to Najd Village. Here is the **menu**.
Thank you. What is good today?
Two kabsa and a salad, please.
Saud, did you see the **documentary** on TV last night?
Yes, I **saw** it. It was about the Royal Saudi Air Force. I **thought** it was **wonderful**.
I thought it was **quite** long, but **interesting**.
It wasn't **boring**! I also **bought** an aviation **magazine** yesterday.
Can I read it after you?
Sure. I **read** half of it last night.
Here is your food. Enjoy your meal!
That was delicious. Excuse me, can we have the **bill**, please?

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 7/FND_68_Week_7_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 7 conversation: Dinner at Najd Village

dialogues.grammar: Did you…? Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
dialogues.title: Did You Enjoy the Trip?
dialogues.setting: A phone call. Yasser calls Mansour back.
lines: Hi Mansour! I got your **voice message**. **Did** you enjoy the **trip**?
Yes, he did. He **drove** for [[two hours]].
Was there a lot of **traffic** on the **road**?
Yes, so we stopped at a **petrol station**.
Yes! We saw [[ten]] camels at my uncle's **farm**.
Yes, we did. We made a **campfire** and watched the **sunset**.
Yes, I **took** [[forty]] photos of the **stars**. Did you study for the test?
No, I **didn't**. I was busy. Let's study together tonight!

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 7/FND_68_Week_7_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 7 conversation: Did You Enjoy the Trip?

dialogues.grammar: Past simple review: got • told • spent
dialogues.title: A Visit to Diriyah
dialogues.setting: Diriyah, near Riyadh. A guide meets Nasser and his father.
lines: Welcome to Diriyah! This is a **famous** **historic** **area**.
Thank you. Are these walls very old?
Yes, they are about three hundred years old. People **made** them from **mud**.
Yes, you can. Do you have your **tickets**?
Great. Please follow me. We can **walk around** for one hour.
Dad, look at the **view** from the **top** of the **tower**!
It's **beautiful**. I can see all of Riyadh.
Can we go to the **souq** after this? I want a **souvenir**.
There is a **museum** near the souq too. Many **tourists** visit it.
Thank you. This is a [[wonderful]] place!

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 8/FND_68_Week_8_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 8 conversation: A Visit to Diriyah

dialogues.title: How Was Jeddah?
dialogues.setting: Monday at college. Ziyad is back from Jeddah.
lines: Welcome back, Ziyad! How was Jeddah?
It was great, but we **only** had one day.
Yes. We **checked in** at [[ten]] in the morning and got our **key** at **reception**.
Yes, we walked there and saw the big **fountain**.
No, we **didn't**. It started to **rain**, and we got **wet**!
Oh no! Did you take a **boat**?
No. **Unfortunately**, the boat trips stopped because of the rain.
Did you eat at the **fish market**?
Yes! The fish was very **fresh**. But I didn't sleep **enough**. I **slept** for only [[five]] hours!
Next time, stay for three days!

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 8/FND_68_Week_8_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 8 conversation: How Was Jeddah?

dialogues.grammar: Wh- questions: Where • When • Who • What
dialogues.title: My Backpack Is Lost!
dialogues.setting: The lost property office at King Khalid Airport. Mr. Saleh is with his son, Rami.
lines: Hello. I lost my **backpack** at the airport yesterday.
It is [[grey]]. It is a **large** backpack with a **name tag**.
I think it was **next to** Gate [[7]].
At about nine o'clock last night.
Please wait… Is this your backpack?
Dad, check the wallet. Is your **passport** there?
Don't worry. It's in my bag. You gave it to me at the gate.
Please **sign** this **form**, and show me your **ID card**.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 8/FND_68_Week_8_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 8 conversation: My Backpack Is Lost!

dialogues.title: My Goals for the Next Exam
dialogues.setting: A learner journal meeting in class.
lines: Hamad, let's look at your **journal**. What is your **strength**?
My strength is **speaking**. I like talking in English.
What is your **target** for the next exam?
That's a good **goal**. Fahad, what about you?
My weakness is **listening**. I want to **improve** it.
Use an English **app**, Fahad. I use one every evening.
Good idea. I also need to **revise** my **vocabulary**.
You are both **hard-working**. I'm **proud** of your **progress**.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 8/FND_68_Week_8_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 8 conversation: My Goals for the Next Exam

dialogues.title: At the Aviation Museum
dialogues.setting: An aviation museum in Riyadh. Mr. Ibrahim's class is on a visit.
lines: Welcome to the **aviation** museum, class. Stay together, please.
Look at that old **aircraft**! It has a **propeller**.
Now let's go to the second **hall**. There is an **exhibition** about the **air force**.
Wow! I can see **fighter jets** and **helicopters**.
Yes, they are. They are from the **history** of the Royal Saudi Air Force.
Yes, you can. And you can try the **flight simulator**.
Amazing! I **flew** a small plane for [[five]] minutes. I **sat** in the pilot's seat!
I **learnt** a lot today. I want to be an [[engineer]].
And I want to be a [[pilot]]!

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 8/FND_68_Week_8_Conversations_A1.pdf
src.label: Week 8 conversation: At the Aviation Museum

listening.title: A New Student
script: Hello, everyone. My name is Bader. That's B-A-D-E-R. I am eighteen years old. I am from Tabuk. Tabuk is a city in the north of Saudi Arabia. Now I live in Riyadh with my brother. I am a student at IATC, in class FND 68. My classroom is Room 105. My teacher is Mr. Adel. He is from Egypt. In my bag, I have an English book, a notebook and two pens. My favourite English word is 'hello'! Thank you. Goodbye!
mc: How many pens does he have?
listening.tip: Spell the name slowly, letter by letter. Revise 18 (eighteen) and 80 (eighty) before Q1.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 1/FND_68_Week_1_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf
src.label: Week 1 listening: A New Student

listening.title: A Family Photo
script: Hi, I'm Yousef. This is a photo of my family. This man is my father. His name is Ibrahim. He is fifty years old, and he is a doctor. This is my mother. She is kind and happy. That tall boy is my brother, Ali. He is twenty. He is a soldier. And that small boy is my brother, Omar. He is only seven. And this is me! I am nineteen, and I am a student at IATC. We are a happy family.
listening.tip: Point to yourself and the class for this / that as you read. Pause after each person.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 1/FND_68_Week_1_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf
src.label: Week 1 listening: A Family Photo

listening.title: Hamad's Day
script: My name is Hamad. Every day, I get up at six o'clock. I pray, and then I have breakfast with my mother. I eat cheese and bread, and I drink tea. I go to IATC by car with my cousin. Our classes start at half past one. At the break, I eat a sandwich and drink water. Classes finish at eight o'clock. In the evening, I walk to the park with my friends. At night, I study English for one hour. I go to sleep at half past ten.
mc: What time does Hamad get up?
Who does he have breakfast with?
How does he go to IATC?
What does he drink at the break?
What time does he go to sleep?
notes: He goes to IATC with his ____
listening.tip: Write the clock times 6:00, 1:30, 10:30 on the board after checking, and say them together.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 1/FND_68_Week_1_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf
src.label: Week 1 listening: Hamad's Day

listening.title: An Announcement
script: Good afternoon, students of FND 68. This is Mr. Hamdan. Please listen. Tomorrow is Thursday. Your first lesson is in Room 115, not Room 212. Room 115 is on the first floor of Building 2. The lesson starts at half past one. The break is at three o'clock. On Thursday afternoon, you have IT in Room 120. Please bring your ID card and a pen. Twenty students in your class have a new book. The other eight students can get the book on Sunday. Thank you, and don't be late.
mc: What do students need to bring?
When can the other students get the book?
listening.tip: Numbers are the focus. Before listening, drill 12 / 20, 15 / 50, 13 / 30.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 1/FND_68_Week_1_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf
src.label: Week 1 listening: An Announcement

listening.title: Three Students, Three Cities
script: Hello, I'm Majed. I'm from Abha. It is a city in the south of Saudi Arabia. It is in the mountains. Now I live in Riyadh with my uncle.
Hi, my name is Khalid. I'm from Al-Ula. It is a small town in the north-west. It is very old and beautiful. I live in Riyadh, near IATC.
Good afternoon. I'm Hassan. I'm from Kuwait, but I live in Dammam, on the east coast. My father works there. Our flat is near the sea.
listening.tip: Change your voice a little for each speaker, and say 'Speaker 1 … Speaker 2 …' clearly.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 2/FND_68_Week_2_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf

listening.title: At the College Office
script: Good morning. What is your first name?
Thank you. How old are you?
I live at 27 King Fahd Street, in Riyadh.
Do you live in a house or a flat?
And what is your father's job?
He is a soldier. My mother is a teacher. Her school is near our flat.
mc: What is the student's first name?
listening.tip: Spell the surname slowly. Accept 'Alharbi' or 'Al-Harbi'.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 2/FND_68_Week_2_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf

listening.title: At the Information Desk
script: Good morning. I work at the information desk at King Khalid International Airport. Today we have visitors from many countries. Mr. Hassan is Egyptian. He speaks Arabic. Mr. Singh is Indian. He speaks Hindi and English. Mr. Raza is Pakistani. His language is Urdu. Mr. Smith is Canadian. He speaks English and French. And Mr. Tanaka is Japanese. They are all engineers for a new airline. Their plane leaves at half past nine from Gate 14.
mc: What time does their plane leave?
listening.tip: Accept small spelling mistakes in nationalities if the word is clear (e.g. 'Canadien').

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 2/FND_68_Week_2_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf

listening.title: A Voice Message from Waleed
script: Hi Omar, it's Waleed. I'm at the mall. I want to buy a phone cover for you. The black cover is twenty-five riyals, and the blue one is nineteen riyals. A new charger is forty-five riyals. How many covers do you want? Please send me a text message. My new phone number is 055 318 2266. That's zero five five, three one eight, double two, double six. The shop closes at eleven o'clock. Thanks!
mc: How much is the blue cover?
What does Waleed want from Omar?
listening.tip: Item 9 is the whole number 318 2266; give 1 mark only if all seven digits are right.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 2/FND_68_Week_2_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf

listening.title: Exam Instructions
script: Good afternoon, everyone. Please listen carefully. The exam is tomorrow, Thursday, in Room 214. Please come at one o'clock. The reading exam is first. It is thirty minutes. Then you have a short break of ten minutes. After the break, you do the writing exam. You need to write twenty-five words. Bring two pencils and your ID card. Phones are not allowed in the room, so put your phone in your bag. Write your name and your student ID on every page. Sleep early tonight. See you tomorrow!
mc: Where do students put their phones?
notes: On every page: your name and student ____
listening.tip: This is practice. If the real exam details are different, tell students the real ones after the task.

listening.title: A Flat for Your Family
script: Hello, Mr. Fahad. This is Majid from Al-Nakheel Homes. I have a flat for your family. It is on the fourth floor of a new building on Olaya Street. It has two bedrooms, one bathroom, a kitchen and a big living room. There is a new sofa and there are two lamps in the living room. The kitchen is small, but it is very clean. The bedrooms have big windows and cupboards. The price is three thousand riyals a month. You can see the flat on Monday at five o'clock. My number is 050 224 6610. Thank you.

What is in the living room?
When can Mr. Fahad see the flat?

script: Hi Ahmed, it's Dad. Please go to the supermarket after college. We need two bags of rice, one chicken and twelve eggs. We also need some vegetables for dinner: tomatoes and potatoes. Don't buy any fruit. We have apples and oranges at home. Buy a big bottle of orange juice for your brother. The supermarket is open until midnight. Take some money from my wallet. It is on the table. Thank you!

How many eggs do they need?

listening.title: A Technician's Day
script: Mr. Faris, you are a technician at King Khalid Airport. What time do you wake up?
I wake up at half past four in the morning.
That's very early! What do you do first?
I pray, I take a shower and I dress. Then I have a small breakfast.
How do you go to work?
I drive. I leave home at a quarter past five, and I arrive at six.
It begins at half past six, and it ends at three in the afternoon.
What do you do after work?
I rest for one hour. Then I play football with my sons.
mc: What time does he wake up?
How does he go to work?
What does he do after he rests?
listening.tip: Revise quarter past / half past with a clock drawing before listening.

src.label: Week 3 listening: A Technician's Day

listening.title: A Sale at City Clothes
script: Hello, shoppers! Welcome to City Clothes. Today there is a big sale. All shirts are now fifty riyals. Dark blue jeans are only eighty riyals. Do you need new shoes? A pair of black shoes is one hundred and twenty riyals. Socks are on the first floor, next to the caps. Three pairs of socks are twenty riyals. There are new winter jackets in large and small sizes. Please ask our staff for help. The shop closes at eleven o'clock tonight. Thank you!

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 3/FND_68_Week_3_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf
src.label: Week 3 listening: A Sale at City Clothes

listening.title: How Do I Get to Your House?
script: Hi Saad. I'm at the petrol station on King Fahd Road. How do I get to your house?
OK. Go straight along King Fahd Road. Turn left at the big mosque.
Turn left at the mosque. OK.
Then go straight. You can see a bank on your right. Turn right after the bank.
My street is Al-Yasmin Street. My house is the third house on the left. It is between a pharmacy and a small park. It has a green door.
Great. See you in ten minutes!

Waleed says: See you in … minutes.
notes: House: the ____ house on the left

src.label: Week 3 listening: How Do I Get to Your House?

listening.title: Jobs Day at College
script: Good afternoon, students. Welcome to our Jobs Day. We have three guests today. Our first guest is Captain Saeed. He is a pilot with Saudia. He flies to Cairo and London every week. Our second guest is Mr. Bader. He is an engineer at a big company in Riyadh. He fixes computers and machines. Our third guest is Dr. Fawaz. He is a doctor at the military hospital. He works at night three times a week. After the talks, you can ask questions. The talks finish at half past five.
mc: How often does Dr. Fawaz work at night?
notes: Captain Saeed flies to Cairo and ____
Dr. Fawaz works at the ____ hospital

listening.title: My Classmate Sultan
script: This is my classmate, Sultan. He is twenty years old, and he comes from Qassim. He lives near the college with his cousin. Sultan gets up at nine o'clock and goes to the gym every morning. He arrives at IATC at one o'clock. His favourite subject is IT, but he likes English too. At the break, he drinks tea and eats dates in the canteen. After class, he studies in the library for one hour. He uses a laptop and a dictionary. Sultan wants to be an engineer.
mc: What time does he arrive at IATC?
notes: Every morning he goes to the ____
He studies in the library for ____ hour
He uses a laptop and a ____

listening.title: A Message from Fahad
script: Hi Saad, it's Fahad. I'm back from the beach in Al-Khobar. The weekend was wonderful! We arrived on Thursday night and stayed in a small hotel near the sea. On Friday morning, the weather was warm and sunny. We walked on the beach and played volleyball. My father cooked fish for lunch. In the afternoon, we swam in the sea for two hours. On Saturday, my brothers and I visited the big mall. We returned to Riyadh at nine o'clock last night. I was very tired! Call me later.
mc: Where was Fahad at the weekend?
When did they return to Riyadh?
notes: On Saturday they visited the big ____

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 4/FND_68_Week_4_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf

listening.title: Nasser's Trip to Al-Ula
script: Hello, I'm Nasser. Three weeks ago, I went to Al-Ula with my two brothers. We drove from Riyadh, and the journey took ten hours! We stayed in a hotel near the old town. We saw big rocks and very old buildings, and we took many photos. On the second day, we met a guide. His name was Mr. Talal. He told us about the history of Al-Ula. The weather was hot in the day and cool at night. We spent four days there, and we came back last Monday.
mc: When did Nasser go to Al-Ula?
How many days did they spend there?
notes: They saw big ____ and old buildings
listening.tip: After checking, list the irregular verbs students heard: went, drove, took, saw, met, told, spent, came.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A0 - A1 Weekly Materials/Week 4/FND_68_Week_4_Listening_A1_Teacher_Version.pdf

listening.title: Safety Talk in the Hangar
script: Good morning, team. Before we start, listen carefully. Today we have some work on two aircraft. First, everyone needs a helmet and gloves. You can't work in the hangar without them. Second, you can't use your phone near the engines. Third, put all your tools back in the tool box after work. We don't want any tools on the runway. listeningExams.grammar: there is / there are • place prepositions

lines: Dad, I can't find my phone. Is it in the car?
No, it isn't in the car. And it isn't under the table.
Oh! Look. It's on the bench, next to the tree.

items.q: Which day do they go to the zoo?
items.focus: days • zoo, crowded
lines: Sultan, let's go to the zoo on Thursday.
Sorry, I'm busy on Thursday. What about Friday?
Friday is very crowded. There are a lot of families.
OK. Let's go on Saturday morning. It's quiet then.

items.q: Where is the café?
items.focus: in front of, under, inside, outside • café, museum, bridge, lake
lines: Excuse me. Is there a café in this park?
Yes, there is. It isn't next to the lake. Walk under the bridge, and you can see the museum.
Is the café inside the museum?
No, it's outside. It's in front of the museum.

items.q: What time does the tower open?
items.focus: times (o'clock, half past) • time trap: last month vs now • tower, view
lines: What time does the tower open? Is it nine o'clock?
No. Last month, it opened at nine o'clock. But now it opens at half past ten.
Half past ten? OK. Let's meet in front of the tower at ten o'clock.
Good idea. The view from the top is beautiful!

items.q: What was the problem with the new restaurant?
items.focus: same meaning, different words: too many people = crowded • modern, stadium
lines: How was the new restaurant near the stadium?
The food was very good, and it wasn't expensive.
No, it's big and modern. But there were too many people. We waited for forty minutes!

items.q: Where do they sit?
items.focus: inside, under, on • bench, grass, tree
lines: It's very hot today. Let's sit inside the café.
Inside is very crowded. Let's sit on the grass.
No, the grass is wet. Look! There's a bench under that tree.
Good idea. It isn't hot under the tree.

sentences.text: My name is Turki, and I live in Riyadh.
Our flat is in a quiet {area} in the north of the city.
In front of our building, there is a big {park}.
There are many tall {trees} and some benches.
In the middle of the park, there is a small {lake} with a bridge.
In the evening, I walk there with my {brothers}.
The park is very {peaceful} in the morning,
but it is {crowded} at the weekend.
Next to the park, there {are} two cafés and a restaurant.
We usually sit {outside} and drink coffee.
From our window, we can see Kingdom Tower.
The {view} at night is beautiful!

p3.title: Nawaf's visit to the museum
p3.focus: Listening for detail: there is / there are, place prepositions (next to, inside, in front of), was / wasn't, didn't
lines: Hi Nawaf. What did you do last weekend?
I went to the National Museum with my cousin, Fahad.
With your cousin? Not your brother?
Yes, it's very big and modern. There are many rooms inside, and there are a lot of old things.
Were you there for thirty minutes?
No, for three hours! There are a lot of things to see.
What is there outside the museum?
Next to the museum, there is a big park with a lot of palm trees.
No, it wasn't. We went in the morning, so it was very quiet.
There is a café inside the museum, but we didn't eat there. We had lunch at a restaurant in front of the park.
That sounds great. I want to go there next weekend.
Go in the morning. It's quiet then.
items: Nawaf went to the museum with his brother.
False
He went with his cousin, Fahad. His brother was busy.
They were at the museum for three hours.
True
"No, for three hours!" (not thirty minutes: number trap 3 / 30)
There is a park next to the museum.
True
"Next to the museum, there is a big park."
The museum was crowded.
False
"No, it wasn't … it was very quiet."
They had lunch inside the museum.
False
There is a café inside, but they had lunch at a restaurant in front of the park.

src.label: A1 Listening Practice Exam · Week 5 Sunday: Places in Riyadh

listeningExams.grammar: always / usually / often / sometimes / never • don't / doesn't • Do…?

example.q: What time does Sami usually get up?
lines: Sami, what time do you usually get up?
I usually get up at half past six.
Half past six? That's early. I get up at seven.

items.q: What time does the college bus come?
items.focus: quarter past • times that sound alike (a quarter past / a quarter to)
lines: Badr, what time does the college bus come?
It comes at a quarter past seven.
No. A quarter past seven. Seven fifteen. Don't be late!

items.q: How often does Khalid go to the gym?
items.focus: How often…? • every day, never • who is speaking? (brother / Turki / Khalid)
lines: Khalid, do you go to the gym every day?
No, I don't. My brother goes every day. I go three times a week: on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday.
I never go to the gym. I don't have time!

items.q: What does Faisal usually have for breakfast?
items.focus: breakfast • usually / sometimes / never • one word or two (eggs / eggs and bread)
lines: Faisal, what do you usually have for breakfast?
I usually have eggs and bread. On Friday, I sometimes have dates and coffee with my father.
Do you drink tea in the morning?
No, I never drink tea in the morning.

items.q: Why is Ziyad late for class?
items.focus: traffic • same meaning, different words: too many cars on the road = bad traffic
lines: Ziyad, you're twenty minutes late. Did you get up late?
No, teacher. I got up at six o'clock, and I took the bus at seven.
There were too many cars on the road. The bus didn't move for half an hour!

items.q: How many minutes is Rakan's drive to college?
items.focus: minute • number trap 13 / 30 • traffic
lines: Rakan, is your home far from the college?
No. By car, it's only thirteen minutes.
No, thirteen. One, three. But I go home at four o'clock, and the traffic is bad then. So the drive home is thirty minutes.

sentences.text: My name is Hamad, and I am an aircraft technician.
I work at an air base near Riyadh, and my day is very {busy}.
I {always} get up at five o'clock.
I {brush} my teeth and pray, and then I have breakfast with my father.
I drive to work, and there is no {traffic} in the early morning.
My work starts at {half} past six.
I check the aircraft for about four {hours}.
At {noon}, I have lunch with my team.
My friend Fahad {doesn't} eat at the base. He brings his lunch from home.
I {return} home at three o'clock.
In the evening, I sometimes go to the gym.
I {never} go to bed after ten o'clock, because I get up early.

p3.title: Faisal's new routine
p3.focus: Listening for detail: frequency adverbs, don't / doesn't, times (a quarter past one), before / after, now vs before
lines: Faisal, how is your new routine at IATC?
It's good, but it's different. Before, I got up at nine o'clock. Now I get up at half past six.
Yes, I always have breakfast. My mother prepares it.
How do you go to college?
I don't drive. My father takes me at noon, and I take the college bus home.
At a quarter past one. But I often arrive early and study in the library.
Do you go to the gym?
Sometimes, on Monday and Wednesday. But I never go at night.
I do my homework every day after dinner, for one hour. Then I use my phone to learn new words.
Thanks. But I'm always tired on Thursday!
items: Faisal gets up at nine o'clock now.
False
"Before, I got up at nine … Now I get up at half past six." (time trap: before vs now)
Faisal's father takes him to college.
True
"My father takes me at noon." He takes the college bus home.
His lessons start at a quarter past one.
True
"At a quarter past one."
He goes to the gym every night.
False
Sometimes, on Monday and Wednesday. "I never go at night."
He does his homework before dinner.
False
"I do my homework every day after dinner."

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A1 Exam/A1 Listening Exam/Week 5/
src.label: A1 Listening Practice Exam · Week 5 Monday: Daily Routine

listeningExams.grammar: comparatives: taller than, faster than, better than

lines: Omar, what's your favourite sport? Is it basketball?
No. I like basketball, but my favourite sport is football.

items.q: What was the score?
items.focus: match, score, won, goal • first vs later (two–one, then three–one)
lines: Fahad, did you watch the college match yesterday?
Yes! We won three goals to one.
Three–one? I heard it was two–one.
At first, it was two–one. Then Ziyad scored again. So it was three–one!

items.q: Who is faster than Nawaf?
items.focus: comparatives: faster than, taller than, slower than
lines: Nawaf, you are fast, but Ziyad is faster than you.
Yes, Coach. But I'm taller than Ziyad!
That's true. And Hamad is slower than both of you.

items.q: What must Rakan NOT eat?
items.focus: healthy, weight, sugar, salad • negative: don't eat
lines: Coach, I want to lose weight. What can I eat?
Eat a lot of salad and fruit. You can eat chicken too.
No. Don't eat sweets. They have a lot of sugar. They're bad for your body.

items.q: When is the next match?
items.focus: days • time trap: last week vs next week • cup
lines: Sultan, when is our next match? Is it this Thursday?
No. We played on Tuesday, and that was last week. The next match is next Wednesday, at five o'clock.
Next Wednesday? Great. We can win the cup!

items.q: How many minutes does Abdullah run every morning?
items.focus: run, exercise, heart • number trap 15 / 50 • who is speaking? (brother)
lines: Abdullah, do you exercise every day?
Yes. I run every morning for fifteen minutes.
No, fifteen. One, five. It's good for my heart. My brother runs for fifty minutes!

sentences.text: My name is Faris, and I play basketball for my college team.
Basketball is my {favourite} sport.
I am {taller} than my brothers, so I am good at it.
We practise with our {coach} three times a week.
Last month, we {won} the college cup.
Our best {player} is Hamad.
He is faster than me, and he never stops.
To stay healthy, I {run} every morning.
I eat a lot of {salad} and fish.
I don't eat much {sugar}.
Exercise is good for your {heart} and your body.
Now I feel {better} than last year.

p3.title: Badr joins the team
p3.focus: Listening for detail: comparatives (faster than), every day vs on Monday and Thursday, times, days (practice day vs match day)
lines: Hello. Do you want to join the college football team?
Yes, Coach. I played for my school team for three years.
Yes. I'm faster than my friends, but they are taller than me.
That's OK. Football players don't need to be tall. Do you exercise every day?
Not every day. I go to the gym on Monday and Thursday.
Our team practises three times a week: on Sunday, Tuesday and Wednesday, at four o'clock.
Four o'clock? My lessons finish at half past three, so that's fine.
Good. And remember: no sugar and no fast food before a match.
OK, Coach. When is the next match?
Next Saturday. We play against Dammam College for the cup.
Great. I want to win that cup!
items: Badr played for his school team for three years.
True
"I played for my school team for three years."
Badr is taller than his friends.
False
He is faster than his friends, "but they are taller than me."
Badr goes to the gym every day.
False
"Not every day. I go to the gym on Monday and Thursday."
The team practises at four o'clock.
True
"…on Sunday, Tuesday and Wednesday, at four o'clock."
The next match is on Sunday.
False
"Next Saturday." Sunday is a practice day (trap).
