listeningExams.grammar: past simple: irregular verbs • didn't + verb • Did you…?

example.q: What did Turki get as a gift?
lines: Nice watch, Turki! Is it new?
Yes. My uncle gave it to me. It was a gift for my graduation.

items.q: When was the graduation ceremony?
items.focus: graduation, ceremony, special • time trap: yesterday vs last Thursday • Did you…?
lines: Nawaf, was your brother's graduation yesterday?
No, it wasn't. Yesterday we had a family dinner. The ceremony was last Thursday.
Yes, I did. It was a very special day.

items.q: Who sent Faisal a message?
items.focus: send / sent, message, say / said • didn't • who did it?
lines: Faisal, did your cousin send you a message after the exam?
No, he didn't. But my teacher sent me a message. He said, "Well done!"
My brother called me. He didn't write a message.

items.q: How many guests came to the dinner?
items.focus: guest, invitation, come / came • number trap 13 / 30
lines: Ziyad, how many guests came to the dinner for your grandfather?
My father sent thirty invitations, but only thirteen guests came.
It rained a lot that night!

items.q: What didn't they eat?
items.focus: eat / ate, have / had, drink / drank • didn't
lines: Fahad, what did you eat at the restaurant after the ceremony?
We had rice and chicken, and we drank orange juice.
No, we didn't. My father doesn't like fish. But we had dates and coffee at the end.

items.q: How did Sultan's father feel?
items.focus: proud, surprise, prize, hear / heard, know / knew • who felt what?
lines: Sultan, did you hear the news? You won the prize for the best student!
Really? I didn't know! I'm very surprised.
Your father was at the ceremony. He told everyone, "I'm very proud of my son."

sentences.text: Last year, my grandfather went to Makkah for Hajj.
When he came home, it was a very {special} day for our family.
I {woke} up early and helped my mother in the kitchen.
We {made} Arabic coffee and put dates on the table.
Many {guests} came to our house.
My uncle {came} from Jeddah by plane.
We {heard} the car at four o'clock and ran to the door.
My grandfather {gave} us small gifts from Makkah.
He {told} us about his trip.
sentences.focus: tell / told vs say / said (tell + person)

sentences.text: We {didn't} sleep before midnight.
I {sent} a photo of him to my friends.
It was a wonderful day.

p3.title: Badr's surprise
p3.focus: Listening for detail: past simple (passed, told, made, gave), didn't, was / wasn't, numbers (twenty minutes), old vs new
lines: Hi Badr. Did you pass your driving test?
Yes, I did! I passed on Monday.
A little. I was worried, but the test wasn't long. It was only twenty minutes.
Did your family know about the test?
No, they didn't. I didn't tell them. I wanted to give them a surprise.
Well, my brother saw my message to my friend, and he told my father!
Then, in the evening, my family made a surprise dinner for me. My cousins came too.
That's nice. What did you eat?
We ate kabsa, and my grandmother made a cake.
Did your father give you a gift?
Yes. He gave me the key to his old car!
Wow! Now you can drive me to college!
items: Badr passed his driving test on Monday.
True
"Yes, I did! I passed on Monday."
The test was very long.
False
"The test wasn't long. It was only twenty minutes."
Badr told his family about the test.
False
"I didn't tell them." His brother told his father.
His cousins came to the dinner.
True
"My cousins came too."
His father gave him a new car.
False
He gave him the key to his old car.

src.doc: FND68/CLass FND 68/A0 - A1 Resources/A1 Exam/A1 Listening Exam/Week 5/
src.label: A1 Listening Practice Exam · Week 5 Wednesday: A Special Day

listeningExams.grammar: on / in / at • some / any • mine / yours • Whose…?

example.q: What does Sami want to join?
lines: Sami, do you want to join the computer club with me?
No, thanks. I want to join an online English course.

items.q: What is Omar's email address?
items.focus: email, address • number trap 15 / 50
lines: It's Omar, fifteen, at mail dot com.
No, fifteen. One, five. Omar, one, five, at mail dot com.

items.q: When does the photo club meet now?
items.focus: club, member, free • on + day, at + time • time trap: last month vs now
lines: Faris, when does the photo club meet? On Monday?
Last month, it met on Monday. But now it meets on Tuesday, at four o'clock.
Tuesday at four. OK, I'm free then.

items.q: Whose phone is on the table?
items.focus: mine / yours • Whose…? • the teacher's
lines: No, it isn't mine. Mine is in my bag. Maybe it's the teacher's.
No, the teacher's phone is black. This one is blue.
Look, there's a photo of Ali on it. It's Ali's!

items.q: What do students do first in the exam?
items.focus: instructions, carefully, underline, key word, mistake • first / then / at the end
lines: Before the exam starts, listen carefully. First, write your name and student ID.
Then do we read the instructions?
Yes. Then read the instructions carefully and underline the key words. At the end, check your mistakes.

items.q: Why didn't Badr reply to the email?
items.focus: reply, email, later • same meaning, different words: sick = ill
lines: Badr, I sent you an email on Sunday. Why didn't you reply?
Sorry, Sultan. I wasn't busy, but I was sick. I stayed in bed for two days.
Oh, I'm sorry. Are you better now?
Yes, thanks. I can read your email later today.

p2.title: A message from the English club
p2.speaker: Hamad

sentences.text: Hello, everyone. This is Hamad from the college English club.
I have some good {news} for you.
Next month, we are starting a new {course}.
The lessons are {online}, so you can study at home.
They are {on} Sunday and Tuesday.
Each lesson starts {at} seven o'clock in the evening.
There are thirty places for new {members}.
The course is {free} for IATC students.
To join, please send me an {email}.
Write your name and student number {carefully}.
Please {reply} before Thursday.
I hope to see you there. Thank you!

p3.title: Sami and Khalid make a plan
p3.focus: Listening for detail: free / busy, on + day, at + time, mine / yours, some / any, morning vs evening
lines: Hi Khalid. I read your email. Thanks for the photos!
You're welcome. Are you free next weekend?
I'm busy on Friday. I have a family lunch. But I'm free on Saturday.
Great. Let's meet at the café near the college.
Which café? There are two cafés there.
The small one, next to the bookshop. At ten o'clock in the morning.
OK. Can you bring your laptop? Mine is broken.
Sure. I can show you some videos from the computer club.
Do you have any videos about planes?
Yes. Last week, I made one about an old plane at the museum.
Cool! And I have some news too. I joined a course.
An online English course. It's every Monday evening.
Good for you! See you on Saturday.
items: Sami is free on Friday.
False
"I'm busy on Friday … But I'm free on Saturday."
They want to meet at the café next to the bookshop.
True
"The small one, next to the bookshop."
Khalid's laptop is broken.
False
Sami's laptop is broken: "Mine is broken." (mine / yours trap)
Khalid made a video about a plane.
True
"Last week, I made one about an old plane at the museum."
Sami's course is on Monday mornings.
False
"It's every Monday evening."
